references.text: God asks sarcastically where the foreign gods are that the people trusted and challenges them to help – the same ironic point as in Judges 10:14.
Elijah mocks the prophets of Baal and tells them to cry out louder to their god, similar to the Lord's sarcastic call to cry out to the false gods.
Isaiah points out that idols cannot save, unlike the living God – the same theme as the Lord's words in Judges 10:14.
Jeremiah asks the same question: where are the gods you have made? Let them rise up and save you if they can.
God says that Judah's towns may cry out to the gods they sacrifice to, but they will not be able to save them in time of trouble.
Israel remembers how they cried out to the Lord in their distress, and He reminded them of earlier deliverance – the context for God's rebuke.
Moses describes how Israel abandoned God and chose foreign gods, which is the background for the Lord's sarcastic words.
